column1: # Targets for the cases in bench/count/cases, one row per case, ranked by score (largest first).
# Counts are instructions per loop iteration from bench/count/count.sh (callgrind; the 22000-iteration run minus the 2000-iteration run, divided by 20000).
# php = PHP 8.6.0RC5. p8 = main 163ee87c. Measured 14 Nov 2026 on addis.

# ops = p8 operations executed per iteration of the case's loop, the callee's included (read from `p8 --dump`; a method body is counted from the same body written as a function, because --dump does not print methods).
# target = php + 10 * ops. gap = p8 - target.
# wp_count = how many times one WordPress request (the scoreboard's) does what one iteration of the case does. wp_cost = what the named routine costs in that request, in instructions.

#   Both come from main 163ee87c: per-function numbers from the scoreboard's callgrind profile; per-operation numbers (an "arm": its runs, and the loop code reached only from it) from a jump-level callgrind run of the same binary.
#   That request executes 10,469,467 p8 operations in 1,280,973,648 instructions; PHP 8.6 takes 525,870,160.

# score = gap * wp_count. It is an upper bound on what reaching the target would save in WordPress: gap covers the whole iteration, not only the named routine. Rows that name the same routine do not add up.
# status: open | claimed: <branch or PR> | merged: <PR> | at target | waits for the rebuild (plain calls: dispatch and the frame restart on calls are not part of the targeted loop).
# before, after = the case's p8 count before and after the merged change. wp_change = that merge's change in WordPress execution.
# Not covered by any case (runs per request, own cost): P8_FREE 1,908,710 (22.9M); P8_MOVE_REG 578,835 (22.7M); P8_JUMP_COND_F and _T 920,991 (13.6M); P8_ASSIGN_TAKE 505,457 (13.2M);
#   P8_FETCH_PROP_IS_THIS and _REG 321,086 (24.6M); P8_FETCH_DIM_IS_REG and _KSTR 161,289 (8.6M); the four return arms 323,459 (56.9M, part of every call case).
